sections.html:
Talbot County is quiet, hilly country in west central Georgia, with Talbotton as the county seat. Besides Talbotton, the municipalities are Woodland, Geneva and Junction City, and a piece of Manchester reaches in. Box Springs is a census-designated place, while Po Biddy Crossroads, Tax Crossroads and Centerville are unincorporated names that turn up on deeds. Population is 5,709, about 15 per square mile.

Most occupied homes here belong to the people living in them, 79.6%, and the midpoint value of such homes is $117,100. Renters pay a midpoint gross rent of $816. No building permits were issued in 2025 and the average commute is almost 43 minutes, so people live here and drive elsewhere for work while nobody adds houses. Nearly three in ten residents are past 65, so estates often put houses up for sale, and an heir meets the tax office before a buyer ever signs.

sections.h2: Where to get tax questions answered
sections.html:
The tax commissioner works from 38 South Jefferson Avenue in Talbotton and receives letters at P.O. Box 147. The office is open weekdays from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm with a noon closure, and the phones are 706-665-3240 and 706-665-3280.

  • Tax commissioner: billing, collections, mobile home titles, timber tax, tax sales.
  • Tax assessors at 706-665-3377: value, returns, exemptions, appeal paperwork.
  • Commissioners' office, 35 Madison St., 706-665-3220: mobile home location permits.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: intangible tax on recorded loan documents.

You can pay with cash, a check, a money order, or a Visa, MasterCard or Discover card, though card payments carry an added fee. The county's qPublic site lets you look up a parcel by owner or address.

Real and personal property statements typically arrive in October and fall due December 20. Part-payments are welcome. After the deadline, interest accrues at prime plus 3%, and every 120 days a further 5% penalty is added until the total hits 20%.

Mobile and manufactured homes follow a January-to-April rhythm. Statements usually go out early in the year with an April 1 deadline, a decal is handed over once the tax is paid, and the return for a home in the county on January 1 is also due April 1. Filing late costs a 10% penalty.

Starting January 1, 2026, the garbage collection fee is $225.00 per year, with extra carts at $137.00 per year. Ask the office whether that charge rides on your parcel's account so the closing agent includes it.

Standing trees escape tax until sold or cut, and then 100 percent of fair market value is multiplied by the millage rate. There are three kinds of timber event.

  • Lump sum sale: the purchaser fills out form PT-283T and delivers form and tax to the commissioner inside five business days, and is personally liable if the seller fails to pay.
  • Unit price sale: a quarterly report goes to the seller and the assessors 45 days after each quarter closes.
  • Owner harvest: the landowner reports to the assessors 45 days after the quarter and pays the tax.

If you have cut or plan to cut trees, ask the office whether a timber account is open before you list.

The commissioner runs levy sales under Title 48 and Title 9 of the Georgia code. A parcel is advertised in the Talbotton New Era for four straight weeks, then auctioned on the first Tuesday of the month after the notices end.

  • Location and time: the courthouse on South Washington Avenue, 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • The county gives no title guarantee, and the bidder gets no access to the property and no rent for at least a year.
  • The high bidder pays in cash or certified funds as soon as the sale ends.
  • Money left after taxes and costs becomes excess funds, claimed by written request to 38 South Jefferson Avenue.

The commissioner's website has a guide to the right of redemption. An owner in arrears has time before the auction, and settling the account in a private sale may leave more equity with the seller.

A disputed value starts with a written filing to the Board of Assessors that names the route you want: Board of Equalization, Superior Court, arbitration, or hearing officer. The postmark must fall no later than 45 days after the notice was mailed.

A real estate return is due between January 1 and April 1 whenever something changed, and omitting a required one costs 10% of the unreported value. Personal property returns, form PT-50P, are filed yearly by April 1.

Exemptions go through the tax assessors. April 1 is the cutoff for the current year, and later filings roll to the next. Forms are accepted all year. Georgia's statewide exemptions apply here, and no local homestead exemption is added on top. An approved exemption renews itself until the owner moves or ownership changes.

Request a written payoff for each year still open, adding mobile home and timber accounts where they exist. With an inherited house, learn which years went unpaid before you list, since a recorded lien has to be paid at the table.

Refunds are narrow. A written request for tax paid in error goes to the Board of Commissioners within three years, and refunds are tied to errors of fault, not to a quarrel over value. Dividing the year's bill between buyer and seller happens on the settlement statement.

With so little building and a small buyer pool, a house with a tax cloud is harder to place. A cash buyer who accepts the house as it stands can pay the balance out of your proceeds at closing. That skips the repair list and the wait on a lender, which matters most when an auction date is close.

Before you call the office, gather the parcel number, any mobile home title, and a note of whether timber has been cut. Ask for payoff figures in writing, and send them to your closing agent so every account is cleared when the deed records.

faqs.q: What is the Talbot County tax commissioner's address?
faqs.a: The office is at 38 South Jefferson Avenue in Talbotton, with P.O. Box 147 for mail. Weekday service runs 8:00 am to 4:30 pm, with a closure from noon to 1:00.

faqs.q: When are Talbot County property tax bills due?
faqs.a: December 20 for real and personal property, with statements typically mailed in October. Mobile home bills fall due April 1.

faqs.q: Does Talbot County accept partial tax payments?
faqs.a: Yes. Interest and penalties still build on the remainder after the due date.

faqs.q: When do Talbot County tax levy sales happen?
faqs.a: They take place on a first Tuesday, once four weeks of Talbotton New Era notices have run, at the courthouse on South Washington Avenue between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: What is the Talbot County homestead exemption cutoff?
faqs.a: April 1 for the current billing year. Forms are accepted all year, and a later one applies to the following year.
